name: centrifugal_compressor_design_similarity
title: Centrifugal compressor design and similarity (air)
summary: Design of a centrifugal turbocompressor from the flow factor and the enthalpy factor of its best-performance point (dry air, 1 bar / 20 C to 2.5 bar, 6000 m3/h): impeller diameter, rotation speed, tip speed and inlet area. A variant applies the same similarity factors to a compressor of the same type compressing methane.

authors: TBD (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory, course Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition of 2004-10-12, exercise 4; individual author not identified)
origin.course: ULiège, Machines et systèmes thermiques, repetition 4 (2004-10-12), exercise 4

verification.reference: EES stored solution of thermo_models TM-0057 (MSTH_041012_exercice_6.EES, EES 7.210, 15 variables, internally consistent run) for the main file, and of TM-0058 (MSTH_041012_exercice_6_suite.EES) for the methane variant; tools/compare_solution.py, no unit conversion needed (SI-C-Pa-J)
verification.notes: Main file: 12 of 15 comparable variables agree within 0.031 % (DELTAh_s 0.0304 %, A and U 0.015 %, N and rpm 0.023 %); the 3 remaining are the absolute enthalpies/entropy, offset by the EES-7 vs CoolProp reference states (+125.87 kJ/kg on h, -1814.9 J/kg-K on s, as for CSL-0023 and CSL-0035), all energy differences agree. Methane variant: 12 of 15 comparable variables agree within 0.0026 % (DELTAh_s 2.6e-05), same reference-state offsets on h and s. No unit conversion needed (SI-C-Pa-J). Both files need their .initials with the Newton-only default pipeline (the example's SOLVER NOTE about TrustRegion does not hold for a CLI run); see README.
